User guide

Effects and automation

Double-click an event (or choose Effects… in its menu) to open its effects window. A linked pair opens as one window with a section for the picture and one for the sound.

The chain

The top row of each section is the chain: a master switch, then one slot per effect with its own switch and a cross to remove it. Drag slots to reorder them. + effect… opens the picker, Preset… saves or applies a whole chain, Copy the chain and Paste the chain move chains between events (curves included). The first slot of a video event is Geometry — position, zoom, rotation, crop and anchor — and it cannot be removed.

The picker is a gallery: each video effect and each preset variant is previewed on the event's own frame. Type to filter.

Video: Geometry, Mirror, Corner Pin, Blur, Sharpen, Radial Blur, Greenscreen, Drop Shadow, Edges, Noise, VHS, Event Grid, Vignette, Pixelate, Halftone, Glow, Pan 3D, Cylinder 3D, Color Grade, Duotone, Posterize, Chromatic Aberration, Lens Distort, Twirl, Ripple, Kaleidoscope — and Slowed+Reverb, which slows the picture too.

Audio: Gain, Slowed+Reverb, Pitch Shift, Filter, EQ, Distortion, Bitcrusher, Tremolo, AutoPan, Vibrato, Chorus, Flanger, Phaser, Delay, Compressor, Gate, Limiter, Stereo Width. Effects that look ahead (the limiter, pitch shift) are latency-compensated, so the sound stays in sync with the picture.

Slowed+Reverb

  • Rate slows the material (0.86 is a classic "slowed" feel).
  • Mix sets how much reverb is heard.
  • Delay, Damp, Decay, Wet, Pre-delay and Width shape the reverb itself.

On a linked pair the picture slows down with the sound. The video side has its own switch in the chain, so you can slow only the sound.

The rate is a real time map. The event's filmstrip and waveform show the material it actually plays, and the timeline cursor stays in sync with them.

Automation curves

Any numeric parameter can change over time:

  1. Press + curve under the parameters and pick the parameter. It appears as a coloured button above the graph.
  2. Click on the graph to add keys and drag them with the mouse. The parameter field always shows the value at the playhead; editing the field edits the key under the playhead.

  3. Each key sets the shape of the segment after it:

    • linear, smooth, ease in, ease out;
    • hold (a step);
    • zigzag (triangle, square or sine, with periods and amplitude);
    • a formula.

    A curve can also be linked to another property, with an expression.

  4. Switch Graph / Table to edit the same keys as numbers.
  5. Copy the envelope / Paste the envelope move curves between parameters, events and even different effects. Matching fields are pasted silently; for the rest you choose.

Keys are stored in the time of the source material. Trimming or moving an event never shifts its automation relative to the picture.

The same curves drive transitions, generators (an animated title is just curves on the title), the Geometry node and published reel parameters.

Track effects and ducking

Every track has its own chain in the track window (right-click the header). The compressor has a sidechain key: put it on the music track, key it from the dialog track, and the music ducks under speech — that is the Audio ducking section of the track window.
